html:
The Desana, who call themselves Umukomasã, are a Tukanoan people of the Vaupés region on the border of Colombia and Brazil, living along the Papurí and Tiquié rivers in the Amazon forest.

Like their neighbours the Wanano and the Cubeo, they marry outside their own language group, so most households speak several languages. They grow manioc and fish, and trade with forest foragers such as the Hupda. Their beliefs became widely known through the work of the anthropologist Gerardo Reichel-Dolmatoff. Missionaries and rubber collectors of the rubber boom reached them from the late 1800s.
